text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian Airlines will increase its captital by 9.92 million litas from 76.53 million litas.
- The privatisation programme for the 99.3-percent state-owned Panevezhys Glass is due in September. The company had a 1996 profit of 8.47 million litas on turnover of 98.56 million litas.
- Lithuanian Railway reported a 2.2 million litas profit versus 5.05 million litas loss in the same period last year.
- A group of prominent Lithuanian industrial leaders agreed to set up a company to launch a sea port in Shventoji in northwest Lithuania.
- The Bank of Lithuania registered Litimpex's share capital boost to 64 million litas.
- Yarn producer Vernitas reported a 64 percent decrease in turnover in the first half and a loss of 140,000 litas for the month of June.
- The governor of the central bank said Lithuanian commercial banks may be allowed to make loans in foreign currencies for domestic settlements next year.
- Cargo carried by rail increased by 12 percent, 39 percent by river transport and 53 percent by air transport in the first half of the year.
- The former president of Vakaru Bankas, Petras Kravtas, has been arrested in connection with the bankruptcy of the defunct bank.
- Textile producer Linas will start two joint ventures, with Ireland's Linen-Cotton Market Limited and U.S. Positive Influence fashions. Linas exports 90 percent of its production.

- Lithuania observed the seventh anniversary of the brutal killings of seven border guards. The killings, which took place after Lithuania had declared indepence from the Soviet Union, are still unsolved.
